policy_metadata.applies_to: Training, testing, fine-tuning and evaluation datasets used for AI, ML and analytics

policies.review_cycle: Annual or upon material change to privacy, AI or data governance requirements

policies.Purpose: This policy defines mandatory requirements for identifying, flagging and remediating personal data in datasets used for artificial intelligence, machine learning, model fine-tuning, model evaluation and analytics activities.

policies.Scope: all datasets that are proposed for AI or machine learning use, including raw data, curated training data, labelled data, test data, validation data, embeddings, logs, prompts, responses and synthetic data derived from personal data

policies.Policy Objective: Datasets must be assessed before use. Records containing personal data must be flagged. Records containing unresolved personal data must not be used for AI training, fine-tuning or evaluation unless an approved exception is recorded.

policies.Policy definition: Information that identifies, or can reasonably identify, a living individual either directly or in combination with other information.
A data item that can identify an individual on its own.
A data item that may identify an individual when combined with other information.
More sensitive information such as health, ethnicity, religion, political opinion, biometric or genetic information.
Any dataset used to train, fine-tune, evaluate or improve an AI, ML or analytics model.
A dataset record where one or more policy rules identify personal data or suspected personal data.
Action taken to remove, mask, tokenise, generalise or anonymise personal data before dataset use.

policies.direct_identifiers: The following fields are treated as personal data when present in training data and must be flagged.

policies.Examples: address, home_address, street, postcode with address

policies.PII type: Bank account or payment card number

policies.Examples: IP address, device ID, cookie ID, user ID where linkable to a person

policies.sensitive_personal_data: The following fields are treated as sensitive personal data when present in training data and must be blocked unless a documented approval exists.

policies.indirect_identifiers: Some fields may not identify a person on their own but can identify a person when combined with other attributes.
policies.combinations: The following combinations must be flagged as personal data.

policies.Combination rule: Full name + postal address or postcode
Employee ID + department + role where linkable to a person
Customer ID + account event details where the customer can be re-identified

policies.Policy statement: Training data must be scanned for personal data before it is used for model training, fine-tuning, testing or evaluation.
Each record containing direct, sensitive or combination-based personal data must be flagged.
Direct identifiers must be removed, masked, tokenised or replaced before the record is approved for training use.
Sensitive personal data must be blocked from training data unless a documented approval and control justification exists.
Records matching combination rules must be reviewed and remediated before use.
Free-text fields such as comments, notes, feedback and descriptions must be scanned for personal data patterns.
Every remediated record must retain evidence of the remediation method applied.
Only records with no unresolved personal data findings may be included in the approved training dataset.
Exceptions must be documented, risk-assessed, time-bound and approved by the Data Protection Office or delegated authority.
The scan result, triggered rule, decision, remediation status and approver must be retained for audit purposes.

policies.Meaning: No personal data or suspected personal data has been detected.
policies.Required action: Record may be included in the approved training dataset.

policies.Meaning: Direct or combination-based personal data has been detected.
policies.Required action: Record must be remediated before training use.

policies.Meaning: Sensitive personal data or high-risk identifier has been detected.
policies.Required action: Record must be excluded unless approved exception exists.

policies.Meaning: A documented approval allows controlled use of the record.
policies.Required action: Use only under the approved conditions and retain audit evidence.

policies.Policy expectation: Delete the personal data field or remove the record where the field is not required.
Replace part of the value while preserving limited analytical utility, where appropriate.
Replace the identifier with a non-identifying token.
Reduce precision, such as replacing exact date of birth with age band.
Transform data so individuals are no longer reasonably identifiable.

policies.Requirement: Name and version of the dataset assessed.
Date when the dataset was scanned.
List of policy rules triggered by each flagged record.
PASS, FLAG, BLOCK or EXCEPTION APPROVED.
Not required, pending, completed or exception approved.
Named reviewer or approval reference where required.

policies.non-compliance: Datasets with unresolved personal data findings must not be used for AI training, fine-tuning, testing or evaluation.
consequences: other action determined by the organisation

policies.policy_review_frequency: at least annually or when there is a material change to privacy, AI governance, data use, model development or regulatory requirements

policies.Summary of change: Initial student version for AI training data PII policy-as-code exercise.
